confidence_note: Blind confidence numbers were subjective judgments of the supplied fictional evidence and are not calibrated accuracy probabilities or empirical confidence intervals.

Second-pass correction to my blind judgment: changing Pod labels is permitted in some contexts, but a kubelet node identity with NodeRestriction cannot change labels through pod/status. Therefore E3 can explain rejected completion status even though its nodeSelector detail conflates a separate ordinary-update path.
The broad answer-key mechanism is acceptable; rewrite the evidence so a learner does not infer that pod/status rejects nodeSelector through ordinary Pod-spec immutability validation.

proposed_changes.proposed: 19:10Z after CA injection, the webhook matches UPDATE requests for both pods and pods/status. A job-controller ordinary Pod update is rejected because the webhook adds an immutable nodeSelector. Separately, the webhook adds labels to a kubelet pods/status update; with NodeRestriction enabled, admission rejects the label change from the node identity, and completion status never persists.
proposed_changes.purpose: Separate immutable spec validation on ordinary Pod updates from NodeRestriction label validation on kubelet status updates.

proposed_changes.proposed: Fail-open admission during delayed CA injection allowed real-node scheduling; later webhook label mutation of kubelet status updates was rejected by NodeRestriction, blocking completion status and cleanup. sources.finding: DeleteInstanceProfile requires that the profile has no associated role. The documentation warns that deleting a profile associated with a running instance can break its applications.
admitPodStatus rejects a node status update if the old and new Pod labels differ. This explains the ACRL label rejection when this plugin and node identity apply.
podStatusStrategy.PrepareForUpdate restores old Spec. A nodeSelector edit is not by itself evidence of the regular immutable-Pod-spec error on the status subresource.
